intro: Santo Domingo rewards visitors with a mix of history, culture, and Caribbean energy. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro: two lines, RD$20 per ride with smartcard (RD$60 card + RD$20 minimum).
Buses: cheap but confusing; fares around RD$20-40.
Taxis: no meters; agree fare before; apps Uber and InDrive work.
Driving: chaotic; not recommended for short visits.
Walking: best in Zona Colonial and Malecón; sidewalks uneven.
Ferry: to Puerto Rico (Mayagüez/San Juan) about US$200 roundtrip, 12 hours.

ciudad-colonial.name: Ciudad Colonial
ciudad-colonial.price_text: Free to walk · individual sights charge separately
ciudad-colonial.tip: Start at Parque Colon and wander the grid on foot; cobbles are uneven, so wear flat shoes.

alcazar-colon.name: Alcazar de Colon
alcazar-colon.price_text: Small entry fee · check on the day
alcazar-colon.tip: The upstairs rooms and courtyards are the highlight; go early to beat tour groups.

catedral-primada.name: Catedral Primada de América
catedral-primada.price_text: Small entry fee · check on the day
catedral-primada.tip: Dress modestly and keep quiet during services; the stone interior stays cool at midday.

ozama-fortress.name: Ozama Fortress
ozama-fortress.price_text: Small entry fee · check on the day
ozama-fortress.tip: Climb the Tower of Homage for the best river-and-city view in the old town.

faro-colon.name: Faro a Colon
faro-colon.price_text: Small entry fee · check on the day
faro-colon.tip: It is east of the old town, so take a taxi; the monument is huge and best seen at dusk when lights come on.

la-bandera.name: La Bandera
la-bandera.tip: This is a busy local transport and market area, not a tourist sight; go with a local and keep valuables out of sight.

malecon.name: Malecon de Santo Domingo
malecon.tip: Walk or cycle the seafront at sunset; the breeze makes it the coolest part of the city.

national-palace.name: National Palace, Dominican Republic
national-palace.price_text: Free or small fee · check on the day
national-palace.hours: Weekdays, limited visiting hours · check on the day
national-palace.tip: Bring photo ID; entry is by guided visit and hours can change, so confirm before you go.

mercado-modelo.name: Mercado Modelo
mercado-modelo.price_text: Free to enter · souvenirs and food priced per stall
mercado-modelo.tip: Good for crafts and coffee; bargain politely and keep small notes ready.

parque-colon.name: Parque Colon
parque-colon.tip: The main square of the old town; use it as a meeting point and people-watch from a bench.

calle-el-conde.name: Calle El Conde walk
calle-el-conde.hours: Daylight hours; busier in the evening
calle-el-conde.tip: A pedestrian shopping street from the old town to the modern centre; walk it one way and take a taxi back.

zona-colonial-food-tour.name: Zona Colonial food and history walk
zona-colonial-food-tour.price_text: Guided tours roughly DOP 1,500–3,500 per person · check on the day
zona-colonial-food-tour.hours: Tours usually start morning or late afternoon
zona-colonial-food-tour.tip: Book a small-group walk to taste local dishes and hear the history; confirm what food is included.

gazcue-walk.name: Gazcue neighbourhood walk
gazcue-walk.tip: Quiet streets of old houses and embassies between the old town and the Malecon; good for a calm hour.

piantini-dining.name: Piantini dining and nightlife
piantini-dining.price_text: Mains roughly DOP 500–1,500 · check on the day
piantini-dining.hours: Restaurants from midday · bars late into the night
piantini-dining.tip: The modern city's restaurant and bar district; reserve on weekends and take a taxi after dark.

bella-vista-viewpoint.name: Bella Vista waterfront viewpoint
bella-vista-viewpoint.tip: A quieter stretch of the seafront away from the old town; go at sunset for open sea views.

stays.why: Walk to the cathedral, Alcázar and Plaza España. Best for first-timers who want history on foot.
Modern business district with the best restaurants and malls. Quieter nights, short taxi rides to the old city.
Leafy, calm streets between the Colonial Zone and the Malecón. Good value and walkable to both.
Residential area near the Malecón with apartments and mid-range hotels. Easy for longer stays.

food: Start the day with mangú: mashed plantain with eggs, fried cheese and salami. Cheap and filling.
Try Dominican classics: la bandera (rice, beans, meat), sancocho stew and tostones.
Street snacks: empanadas, quipes and chimi burgers. Eat where locals queue; prices are low.
Seafood along the Malecón and in Boca Chica. Ask the price before ordering fish by weight.
Coffee is strong and local. Look for small cafés in the Zona Colonial; a cup is a few hundred DOP at most.
more_time: Add a beach day: Boca Chica is about 30–40 minutes east by taxi or bus. Check conditions on the day.
History buffs can swap a museum for the Faro a Colón and the Columbus sites across the Ozama river.
Take a day trip to Los Tres Ojos caves and the Botanical Garden if you want nature close to the city.
